Hi [~accountid:712020:c0f6fbe7-f5ae-44e2-bb6c-8e5815ace0d9] as already shared over Slack - some additional questions to submit to the procurer: 

*FRÅGA 1: Begränsning av ansvar*
I nuvarande lydelse av punkt 5.1.27 framgår inget uttryckligt tak för trafikföretagets ansvar, vilket i praktiken innebär ett obegränsat ansvar.Punkt 5.1.21 reglerar försäkringsskyldigheten och anger att trafikföretaget ska ha erforderliga försäkringar (inklusive ansvarsförsäkring) ”till betryggande belopp”. Denna bestämmelse skapar dock inte någon faktisk begränsning av det ansvar som kan uppkomma enligt punkt 5.1.27.För att uppnå en rimlig riskfördelning mellan parterna vill vi därför be kommunen överväga att:

* införa en uttrycklig *begränsning av ansvaret* till ett visst skäligt belopp (t.ex. 10 MSEK eller 20 MSEK per skadetillfälle), eller
* alternativt, knyta ansvarsbegränsningen till ett belopp som omfattas av trafikföretagets ansvarsförsäkring enligt punkt 5.1.21.

Kan ni vänligen bekräfta hur kommunen avser att reglera frågan om ansvarsnivå och om en sådan begränsning kan införas?

*FRÅGA 2: Punkt 5.1.27 Ansvar för skada*Vi hänvisar till punkt *5.1.27 Ansvar för skada* i förfrågningsunderlaget. Där framgår att trafikföretaget ansvarar för skada som bolaget, bolagets anställda *(inklusive underleverantörer)*, fordon eller utrustning vållar. Vi vill gärna få förtydligat att denna bestämmelse inte innebär att trafikföretaget övertar *arbetsgivaransvaret för underleverantörers anställda*, utan att leverantörens ansvar gäller att säkerställa att de underleverantörer vi anlitar som juridiska aktörer uppfyller sina åtaganden enligt avtalet. Respektive underleverantör ansvarar själva för sin personal. Vi vill understryka att det inte vore proportionerligt att en leverantör skulle ansvara för en annan juridisk aktörs anställda.Vänligen bekräfta att detta är den korrekta tolkningen. 

*FRÅGA 3: Punkt 5.1.30 Underleverantörer*Vi hänvisar till punkt *5.1.30 Underleverantörer* i förfrågningsunderlaget. Där anges bland annat att:_”Trafikföretaget ansvarar för att underleverantör uppfyller samma krav som ställs på trafikföretaget och a_*_nsvarar för underleverantör som för egen del både vad gäller personal_* _och arbete.”_Formuleringen kan tolkas som att trafikföretaget inte bara ansvarar för att underleverantören uppfyller sina åtaganden enligt avtalet, utan även att trafikföretaget skulle bära *arbetsgivaransvar för underleverantörens personal som om de vore vår egen*.Vi vill understryka att en sådan tolkning:

* inte är proportionerlig, eftersom respektive juridisk aktör måste bära arbetsgivaransvaret för sin egen personal,
* skulle urholka möjligheten att använda underleverantörer i upphandlingen, och
* strider mot grundprincipen att trafikföretaget ansvarar gentemot beställaren för underleverantörens prestation, men inte för arbetsgivaransvar för personal som inte är vår egen.

Mot denna bakgrund ber vi kommunen vänligen bekräfta att avsikten inte är att trafikföretaget ska överta arbetsgivaransvaret för underleverantörers anställda, utan att respektive underleverantör även fortsättningsvis ansvarar för sin egen personal, medan trafikföretaget ansvarar gentemot beställaren för att underleverantören som juridisk aktör uppfyller sina åtaganden enligt avtalet.

From my PoV, launching Bolt Balance in TH, where Bolt Support Services (Thailand) Limited provides RH (i.e., online intermediary services) under a principal status (thus, under the Bolt localized business model) does not trigger any tax implication to deal with because the scope of Bolt Balance will be limited to the *_“wallet functionalities”_*, allowing users to deposit their money in their balance in order to spend it in the usage of subsequent rides. Since the *_“top-up”_* functionality won’t be available, no potential incentives costs will raise in TH.

In addition, Bolt Balance is tied to currency, so users may only deposit money and spend it in the purchase of Bolt products in the TH local currency.

In conclusion, the main function of Bolt Balance in TH will be the usage of such a feature as a payment method, and to enable us to keep a track of credits owed to Bolt by users due to unpaid rides.

[~accountid:6282158fc217e200698b7a4a] I don’t quite follow your tax analysis, but overall I agree there are no tax blockers / risks mainly because passenger transport is not subject to VAT in Thailand 

Bolt Services TH is a limited risk distributor and is the contracting party for the Bolt Platform for both Driver and Passenger app T&Cs. So it is a principal of the Bolt SaaS, but it is still an agent for the passenger transportation.

In scope of its agency granted by the Drivers is the authority to reasonably issue refunds to Riders when there is a complaint to Bolt Customer Support. 

The stated purpose and function for launching Bolt Balance in Thailand is to be able to issue refunds to the Bolt balance, rather than restrictive promotional discount codes; not the usage of the feature as a payment method (although this is possible). [Global Bolt Balance policy|https://bolt.eu/en-th/support/articles/360019507720/] includes the ability to top up the balance to settle failed payments. I don’t see any practical differences between “wallet functionalities” and “top-up” functionality and don’t see why this would be relevant to the analysis (unless trying to determine if exempt financial services are being provided per the _Card Protection Plan_ case)

The difference, for VAT, is that a refund is reimbursed and a promotion code is a Bolt-funded discount that is not reimbursed. As a result, the refund lowers the VAT taxable amount, impacting the driver’s taxable output, while a Bolt-funded discount to the Passenger is a third party subsidy and does not lower the taxable amount of the supply. However, this is not relevant for Thailand because passenger transport is not subject to VAT

The other tax issue I see is whether Bolt Balance could be viewed as a voucher that’s taxable at the time of issuance because it is a specific or single purpose voucher. However, as I understand the Bolt Balance has more of a general or multi-purpose character. Similarly, for Thailand, this is a non-issue because passenger transport is not subject to VAT.

The last issue, for legal, is that the TH terms and conditions will need to be updated to include the Bolt Balance terms, as well as the process for Bolt to be able to claim compensation from the driver for the refunds it issues on the driver’s behalf.  The claimed compensation, as a deduction from the driver’s earnings to cover this, should not be reflected in the commission invoice. Ideally, Bolt will send the driver a compensation claim statement to accompany the driver earnings deduction. Neither the refund nor the reimbursement should hit Bolt’s P&L; only the Balance Sheet.

As a result, I agree - don’t see any tax blockers or any tax risks to launching Bolt Balance in Thailand and suggest that appropriate T&Cs, invoicing and accounting policies are in place as part of the launch

Thank you!

# If a driver previously requested deletion, they must re-register as a new partner.

{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
*Next steps*

* Please do not proceed with granting access for this purpose.
* If there is a specific operational blocker, let’s explore compliant alternatives and discuss further.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*General comment - processing of personal identity codes*
{panel}

The Finnish Data Protection Act permits use of the 11-character personal identity code (hetu) only in narrow statutory situations. Ride-hailing is not on that list. Collecting or storing the full hetu for onboarding or verification would exceed the permitted purposes.

{quote}[_Section 29_|https://www.finlex.fi/api/media/statute-foreign-language-translation/687709/mainPdf/main.pdf?timestamp=2018-12-04T22%3A00%3A00.000Z]

_Processing of personal identity codes_

_A personal identity code may be processed if the data subject has given consent to it or if so provided by law. A personal identity code may also be processed if it is necessary to uniquely identify the data subject:_

# _in order to perform a statutory duty;_
# _in order to implement the rights and duties of the data subject or the controller; or_
# _for scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes._

_A personal identity code may be processed in credit granting and debt collection; in insurance, credit institution, payment service, renting and lending activities; in credit data processing; in healthcare and social welfare services and other activities to ensure social security; and in matters concerning public service employment relationships, employment relationships and other service relationships and benefits relating to these._{quote}



This means we should not capture or store the full identity code in the flow. Recommend speaking to product about designing alternatives such as masking part of the code or using partial verification methods that confirm identity without full retention.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Use of ID documents/code for verification*
{panel}

Regulators have stated that the identity code is not intended to be an identification method. Requesting a copy of an ID document requires strong necessity and proportionality. Storing ID images “just in case” would breach the Finnish data minimisation requirement (we do not delete the ID copies immediately after verifying gender for W4W).


The only way to reduce the risk in Finland is to exclude personal code from verification flows / Explore masking or partial verification options with product. Launching as-is could lead to regulatory scrutiny.



Maybe we can launch W4W without verification in Finland?

58 yearly scheduled block decisions with the outdated logic. Took {{rule_2}} conditions as an example from [BLOCK_BAD_PAYMENT_ORDER|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/rules/edit/driver_period_check/BLOCK_BAD_PAYMENT_ORDER?tab=script&scriptTab=script_view]

!Screenshot 2025-09-03 at 14.56.49.png|width=317,height=257,alt="Screenshot 2025-09-03 at 14.56.49.png"!

{code:sql}WITH stats_per_check AS (
  SELECT 
    ci.created,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN etl.created BETWEEN DATE_ADD('day', -7, ci.created) AND ci.created 
        AND (
          etl.is_payment_problem = TRUE 
          OR etl.is_current_failed_payment = TRUE 
          OR etl.uncovered_amount > 0
        ) 
      THEN 1 ELSE NULL 
    END) AS bad_payment_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN etl.created BETWEEN DATE_ADD('day', -7, ci.created) AND ci.created 
        AND (
          etl.is_payment_problem = TRUE 
          OR etl.is_current_failed_payment = TRUE 
          OR etl.uncovered_amount > 0
        ) 
      THEN etl.uncovered_amount / etl.eur_currency_rate 
      ELSE 0 
    END) AS bad_payment_sum,
    COUNT(CASE 
      WHEN etl.created BETWEEN DATE_ADD('day', -7, ci.created) AND ci.created 
        AND etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
      THEN 1 ELSE NULL 
    END) AS inapp_order_count
  FROM ng_fraud.driver_statistics_check_input AS ci
  JOIN ng_fraud.driver_statistics_check_decision AS cd ON ci.check_id = cd.check_id
  LEFT JOIN ng_fraud.driver_statistics_check_result AS cr 
    ON cr.check_id = ci.check_id 
    AND cr.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('year', -1, CURRENT_DATE) AS DATE)
  JOIN ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl 
    ON etl.driver_courier_id = CAST(json_extract_scalar(ci.input, '$.data.driverId') AS bigint)
  WHERE 
    etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('year', -1, CURRENT_DATE) AS DATE)
    AND ci.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('year', -1, CURRENT_DATE) AS DATE)
    AND cd.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('year', -1, CURRENT_DATE) AS timestamp)
    AND cd.decision = 'SCHEDULED_BLOCK'
    AND cr.strategy = 'BLOCK_BAD_PAYMENT_ORDER'
  GROUP BY 1, CAST(json_extract_scalar(ci.input, '$.data.driverId') AS bigint)
)
SELECT 
  DATE_TRUNC('month', CAST(created AS DATE)) AS month,
  COUNT(created) AS count_unduly_blocks
FROM stats_per_check
WHERE 
    bad_payment_count > 4 AND
    bad_payment_sum < 200 AND
    (bad_payment_count * 1.0) / NULLIF(inapp_order_count, 0) >= 0.5
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 desc{code}

First letter to the supplier:
Sveiki,  

kadangi kyla nesusipratimų dėl Bolt užsakytų paslaugų kainos, norime išsiaiškinti kilusią situaciją.  

Bolt sutinka, kad papildomai buvo užsakytos šios paslaugos: 

* 1h barmenai – 100 EUR; 

* 1h DJ – 120 EUR; 

* 1h autobusas – 60 EUR; 

* 1h fotografas – 100 EUR. 

* taip pat papildomai buvo užsakyti 10 vnt. karštų patiekalų vakarienei. 

 

Pagal 2025-07-25 pasirašytos paslaugų sutarties Nr. RK250725-BO (toliau – *Sutartis*) priedą-užsakymą Nr. 3, šalys susitarė, kad *1 vnt. maisto ir gėrimų komplekto kaina yra 70 EUR*. Prie maisto ir gėrimų komplektų kartu buvo apskaičiuoti ir pietūs, *kurie faktiškai pateikti nebuvo*, tačiau paslaugų teikėjas nurodė, kad vietoje pietų Bolt bus pateikta daugiau užkandžių dienos ir vakaro metu. Bolt taip pat suprato, kad nepanaudoti gėrimai bus išskaičiuoti iš mokėtinos sumos, tačiau tai pateiktoje sąskaitoje-faktūroje neatsispindi.  

Tarp šalių buvo sutarta padidinti vakarienės porcijų kiekį iš 45 vnt. į 55 vnt., Bolt suprantant, kad komplekto kaina, šalių sutarta ir pasirašyta Sutartyje, lieka nepakitusi, t. y. 1 vnt. kaina – 70 EUR, nepaisant to, kad į sumą įeinantys pietūs faktiškai pateikti nebus.

Kadangi Sutartyje numatyta maisto ir gėrimų 1 vnt. komplekto kaina yra 70 EUR, Bolt sutinka už papildomai užsakytą 10 vnt. vakarienės porcijų sumokėti 700 EUR. 

 

Pažymėtina, kad pagal Sutarties 6.1. aiškiai numato, kad „Sutarties sąlygos gali būti keičiamos ir papildomos *tik rašytiniu šalių susitarimu*. Visi Sutarties pakeitimai ir papildymai yra neatskiriama Sutarties dalis ir turi privalomą pobūdį šalims, jei jie yra pasirašyti Užsakovo ir Vykdytojo.”.  

Išskirtina, kad šalys rašytinai nepatvirtino ir nesutiko su kita maisto ir gėrimų 1 vnt. komplekto kaina, todėl Bolt neturi pagrindo sutikti su kita, nei Sutartyje numatyta, paslaugų kaina. Taip pat atkreiptinas Jūsų dėmesys į tai, kad Sutarties sudarymo ir vykdymo metu nuolatos buvo komunikuojamas Bolt biudžetas šiam renginiui, prašoma į jį atsižvelgti siūlant bei teikiant paslaugas. Bolt taip pat ne kartą aiškiai nurodė, kad reikšmingas biudžeto viršijimas nėra galimas, todėl vykdydamas paslaugų sutartį paslaugų teikėjas privalėjo veikti sąžiningai ir protingai, kad tai labiausiai atitiktų kliento interesus (Lietuvos Respublikos civilinio kodekso (toliau – CK) 6.718 str. 1 d.). 

Norime atkreipti jūsų dėmesį, kad vienos šalies sprendimas vienašališkai ir neproporcingai padidinti paslaugų kainą pažeidžia Sutarties šalių susitarimą bei *CK 6.193 str. 1 d.* įtvirtintą principą, kad sutartys turi būti vykdomos sąžiningai ir pagal tikrąją šalių valią. Nors paslaugų apimtis buvo išplėsta, *kainos keitimas turėjo būti suderintas iš anksto ir raštu*, vadovaujantis šalių susitarimo forma bei *CK 6.716–6.722 str.* reglamentuojamais paslaugų sutarčių principais. Nepagrįstas kainos padidinimas pažeidžia *proporcingumo ir sąžiningumo principus (CK 1.5 str.)*, todėl Bolt pagrįstai nesutinka su papildoma paslaugų kaina, kuri skiriasi nuo šalių Sutartimi sutartos paslaugų kainos. 

Tikimės geranoriško ir sąžiningo bendradarbiavimo sprendžiant susiklosčiusią situaciją.  

Jeigu kiltų papildomų klausimų, maloniai prašome kreiptis nurodytu el. paštu.

Reply from the supplier:
*Sveiki,*

 

Atsakau į išsakytas pastabas ir siekiu paaiškinti situaciją dėl maisto bei gėrimų komplektų kainos ir faktiškai suteiktų paslaugų.

Pirmiausiai pabrėžiu, kad Mes kaip Vykdytojas *Jūsų organizuojamame renginyje (pagal 1.1)* punktą teikėme paslaugas. Jūs organizaciniam procesui skyrėte Aušrinę Šlajūtę, kuri pagal pasirašytos sutarties 4.3 punktą turėjo įgaliojimą atstovauti Jūsų pusę derinant detales. Punktas sutartyje skamba taip:

_„4.3. Užsakovo pagal šios sutarties punktą 2.6.1 skiriamas asmuo Aušrinė Šlajūtė (toliau – Atstovas) yra įgaliotas atstovauti Užsakovą derinant paslaugų teikimo ir sutarties įsipareigojimų vykdymo detales su Vykdytoju bei informuojant Vykdytoją apie Užsakovo priimamus sprendimus susijusius su šios sutarties Vykdymu.”_

Taigi, pagal sutartį laikėme, kad derinimas su Aušrine yra pakankamas ir Aušrinė atsakingai ir profesionaliai įsigilina į visą komunikuojamą informaciją kaip Jūsų organizuojamo renginio pagrindinis asmuo. Jūsų biudžeto ribų priežiūra nebuvo mūsų atsakomybė, mūsų atsakomybė suteikti Jums aktualias paslaugas.

 

# *Dėl maisto ir gėrimų komplekto kainos:*

Sutartyje ir jos priede Nr. 3 buvo numatyta preliminari vieno maisto ir gėrimų komplekto kaina – 70 EUR. Buvo aiškiai nurodyta, kad:

_" nurodoma preliminari suma asmeniui - ji gali kisti priklausomai nuo raštu suderinto meniu , kuris derinamas iki 07.28"_.

T.y, aiškiai ir nedviprasmiškai išsakoma, kad galutinė kaina gali būti tikslinama ir derinama atsižvelgiant į galutinai pasirinkto meniu kainą. Pasirašydami sutartį numatėme ir papildomai žodžiu aptarėme, jog maitinimo paslaugų eilutė bus tikslinama vėliau ir tai buvo daroma Jūsų interesui, kad turėtumėte laiko susitikslinti žmonių kiekį išdiskutuoti meniu variantus ir Jūsų poreikius (_Asmeniškai kalbėjau su Aušrine ta tema 2025-07-24 dieną, kadangi sprendžiau renginio vietos užtikrinimo klausimą_).

Maisto derinimas vyko jau po sutarties pasirašymo (užtikrinus sodybą Jūsų renginiui). Kiekvienas meniu variantas buvo siunčiamas Aušrinei su nurodyta kaina. Jūs pasirinkote konkrečius variantus, žinodami kainą, todėl tai laikytina galutiniu susitarimu dėl paslaugų apimties ir kainos. Prisegame paskutinę versiją pasiūlymo, kurį patvirtinote atrašymu.

Meniu derinimo neturite laikyti sutarties sąlygų keitimu (minimų 6.1 punkte), nes kaip sutarties sąlyga ir buvo nurodyta, kad maitinimo kaina „preliminari ir bus derinama vėliau“.

Meniu derinimas yra sutarties vykdymo proceso dalis. Sutarties esmė nekito – abi šalys iš anksto sutiko, kad suma bus „plaukiojanti“. Toks kainos nurodymas maisto eilutėse yra Jūsų interesui, kadangi praktikoje dalyvių kiekiai ir poreikiai kinta iki pat renginio dienos.

*Papildomai pagal punktą 4.2*

_4.2. Jeigu dėl Užsakovo iniciatyvos Vykdytojui prireikia viršyti Sutarties šalių patvirtintą sąmatą ar dėl Užsakovo kaltės atsiranda aplinkybės, kurios padidina išlaidas, Vykdytojas nedelsiant informuoja apie tai Užsakovą ar jo paskirtą atstovą. Patirtos papildomos išlaidos yra įskaičiuoja._

Aušrinės nuomonės ir komentarai derinant meniu žodžiu ir el. laiškais laikytini Užsakovo iniciatyva, mūsų siųsti meniu ir kainos atliepiant Aušrinės iniciatyvas pakankamu ir nedviprasmišku informavimu apie kainos kitimus.

 

# *Dėl gėrimų:*

Po renginio buvo užfiksuota, kad faktiškai sunaudota gėrimų suma yra *72,3 EUR mažesnė* nei preliminariai planuota. Ši suma *jau yra išskaičiuota* iš galutinės sąskaitos.

 

# *Dėl sąžiningumo ir proporcingumo:*

Mes, kaip sutarties Vykdytojas, viso proceso metu veikėme sąžiningai ir skaidriai teikdami paslaugas Jūsų organizuojamame renginyje (pagal 1.1. punktą):

* Buvo pateikiami keli maitinimo pasiūlymo variantai su kainomis;
* Nebuvo taikomas joks vienašalis kainos padidinimas – jūs patys pasirinkote brangesnį meniu;
* Gėrimai, kurie nebuvo sunaudoti, buvo atitinkamai išskaičiuoti;

*Taigi,*

* Meniu kaina buvo suderinta el. laiškais;
* Galutinė suma atitinka faktiškai suteiktas paslaugas;
* Jokie pokyčiai nebuvo daromi vienašališkai – viskas vyko su jūsų žinia, o bandymas interpretuoti kitaip atrodo nesąžiningas.

 

*Kviečiu skubiai apmokėti už suteiktas paslaugas (įskaitant pilna maitinimo kainą), pagal siųstą sąskaitą faktūrą.*

*Jei dar kyla, dvejonių, abipusiškai negaišti laiko ir kalbėtis vadovų lygmenyje, nes susidariusi situacija „nuostolinga/kenksminga“ ne tik pinigų/laiko prasme, bet ir organizacijos įvaizdžių prasme.*

{code:sql}SELECT DISTINCT 
month(co.created) AS MONTH, 
--CASE WHEN co.payment_method_group IN ('cash','business') THEN 'legacy_flow' WHEN co.payment_method_group IN ('family','bolt_credit','in-app') THEN 'balance_flow' ELSE 'other' END AS payment_method_group,
--CASE WHEN COALESCE(co.card_booked_amount,0) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_preauth,
SUM(co.user_price_eur) AS sum_user_price_eur,
COUNT(DISTINCT co.id) AS count_orders,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.uncovered_amount/co.eur_currency_rate) AS double),2) AS fp_sum,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.initial_failed_payment_amount/co.eur_currency_rate) AS double),2) AS initial_fp_sum
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co
WHERE co.created_date BETWEEN date '2025-04-01' AND date '2025-06-30'
AND co.order_type = 'rides'
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
--AND co.payment_method_type NOT IN ('default','business')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 DESC{code}

+*CALL w/ PAULA (03.09)*+

* ‘Device internet app’ is a Bolt-run interface online.

+*API Integration Agreement Review (*+[+*Link*+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1lzd5UdscBhaqDfx2xFbAqBWog0s1TzyH/edit]+*)*+

*REVIEW:*

* Template is between ‘Partner’ (presumably Tapbox) and Bolt Operations OU.
** Third-party partners of the partner are defined as ‘Demand Partners’.
* Partner API access is limited to authorised representatives only (2.7).
* Liability limited to amounts paid under the agreement (5.2).
* Annex 3 contains a DPA and 'data composition requirements.
** Bolt and Demand Partners stated to be independent controllers in respect of the passenger / driver data being shared between them. However, Partner acts as a processor on behalf of the Demand Partner. It is unclear how these fit together.
** Passenger data being transferred from Tapbox to Bolt aligns with my understanding, except the phone number is listed as ‘masked’ and booking reference number is not included.
** Driver data being transferred from Bolt to Tapbox is name, ID number, phone number, vehicle reg / details, driver location and ride status - This does not seem to reflect the facts.
** Contractual obligation for Bolt to process data in accordance with its privacy notice.
** Obligation not to send any unsolicited marketing comms to passengers (surely this increases the ned to disable consents by default).
** Mutual indemnity for data subject claims.

*ANALYSIS:*

* *Processing roles:*
** Unless absolutely necessary, it would be better to characterise Tapbox as a processor here. This is because, even though Tapbox first collects the data:
*** Bolt is deciding on what personal data to collect and the purposes of processing.
*** It is unclear what purposes Tapbox will need the data for themselves. It would be better to ensure that the data is just being used by Bolt to fulfil rides, to prevent any passenger complaints down the road - this can be most easily achieved through data processor terms.
*** The Bolt brand is what the passenger will be faced with, and so the passenger will send any complaints to Bolt. As such, we want to make sure we have a tight leash on Tapbox in case they do anything untoward with the data.
** As such, {color:#4c9aff}*Article 28 term*{color}s would be helpful (subject to role confirmation). We also want {color:#4c9aff}*tighter controls*{color} on what Tapbox can use the data for.
** If Tapbox needs the data for analytics purposes, then we can allow that as an IC position, but this should be made clear to the passenger.
* *Indemnity*:
** Should {color:#4c9aff}*include more than just data subject claims*{color}.
** {color:#4c9aff}*Push for a pro-Bolt indemnity*{color} in the first instance - our name is on it and so we have more to lose (even though we are receiving more data than we are sending). Also, we do not have much of an idea of Tapbox’s security measures.
* *Other:*
** Would be better to use our standard template here, as (i) better clarity on data processing; and (ii) better security in terms of provisions. {color:#4c9aff}*Include this*{color}.
** Bolt should not be agreeing to process in accordance with its privacy notice. This is legally required - not point adding an extra contractual hook. {color:#ff5630}*Remove this*{color}.
** {color:#4c9aff}*Get InfoSec to review*{color} Tapbox.

*QUESTIONS:*

* Where did we get this wording from? Has Privacy Team ever reviewed this?
* ‘Partners’ vs. ‘Demand Partners’? Who are the latter - are they based in the EU? Also, who came up with allocation of controller / processor roles?
* Why have we said that Bolt will be sharing all these driver categories of data with Tapbox?

Hi [@michael.kaiserauer|https://bolt.enterprise.slack.com/team/U04N4AZSBRP] - this is a duplication of the given advice in Slack ([https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C01NM7WP3MW/p1756895310321549|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C01NM7WP3MW/p1756895310321549|smart-link] ) for audit trail:

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Recommendation:* you can proceed “as is” without third party consent considering low risk - but to ensure the risk is minimised, please try to narrow campaign where possible  - i.e. Berlin only, Bolt-focused, and ideally via push or in-app. Use email/SMS sparingly or not at all to minimise complaint and enforcement risk.
{panel}

*Details:*

* *Classification:* the comms could be considered *first-party marketing* (Bolt promoting its own services), even though it references the IFA partnership . This would mean that soft opt-in is possible and this can be categories as "Promotions and trips".
** *Why:* the main offer here is Bolt’s own mobility services with a discount. While this indirectly promotes the IFA event, the primary purpose and benefit being advertised is Bolt’s service, which supports the first-party classification and makes soft opt-in possible.
* *Regulatory risk:* Because the IFA tie-in is explicit, privacy regulator _could_ argue it this third party marketing requiring consent, especially considering that under the surface, is an official partnership with cross-promotion intent. This is why we want to avoid complaints and subsequent questions from regulators, not to get engaged into this dispute.
* *Risk level:*
** Real enforcement risk is *low* if the campaign is limited to in scope (i.e. only in Berlin) and channels.
** Push notifications are very low-risk as people do not usually complain about them; in-app banners do not create any risk at all.
** Emails and SMS carry higher complaint risk in Germany, where regulators are active and will likely pursue spam cases triggered by individual complaints.

Internal note:

Art. 42 of the Spanish Commercial Code:

_A group exists when a company holds or may hold, directly or indirectly, control over one or more other companies. In particular, control shall be presumed to exist when a company, which shall be deemed the parent, is in relation to another company, which shall be deemed the subsidiary, in any of the following situations:_

_a) It holds the majority of voting rights._
_b) It has the power to appoint or remove the majority of the members of the administrative body._
_c) It may, by virtue of agreements entered into with third parties, exercise the majority of voting rights._
_d) It has appointed, with its votes, the majority of the members of the administrative body, who hold office at the time the consolidated accounts are to be prepared and during the two immediately preceding financial years. In particular, this circumstance shall be presumed when the majority of the members of the administrative body of the dominated company are members of the administrative body or senior management of the parent company or of another company controlled by the latter. This situation shall not give rise to consolidation if the company whose directors have been appointed is linked to another in any of the cases set out in the first two subparagraphs of this section._

_For the purposes of this section, to the voting rights of the parent company shall be added those it holds through other subsidiaries or through persons acting in their own name but on behalf of the parent company or of other subsidiaries, or those over which it has control in concert with any other person._

We reached a decision in this thread [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C07K3UZS4G7/p1756900269150439|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C07K3UZS4G7/p1756900269150439|smart-link]  that we will proceed with the option of hard coding the formula on the pricing back-end side. 

I reviewed the formula that is being used currently by the local teams ([source Google sheet|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1jTzGIRX8V3bsWBPEz5WkMeBffMlnClAcDPKDF4n6JnA/edit?gid=1129435239#gid=1129435239], tab Riga - City - Read only, column “Courier Earnings - Planned”).

The formula is essentially the following:

For each $[zone]:

For each $[day_of_week]:

For each $[hour_of_day]:

Expected orders = average order count for the previous four weeks for that $[day_of_week], $[hour_of_day] and that $[zone]. The zone is based what is used for courier pricing - meaning the location of the courier where he got the order proposal

Pickup distance = average pickup distance for the previous four weeks for that $[day_of_week], $[hour_of_day] and that $[zone]

Drop-off distance = average drop-off distance for the previous four weeks for that $[day_of_week], $[hour_of_day] and that $[zone]

Expected courier earnings = our usual courier earnings formula, considering the city and zone multipliers for this zone, and the average pickup and drop-off distances we calculated for the past 4 weeks

Final CPO = weighted average of the Expected courier earnings for all zones, hours and days, where the weights are the expected orders for that zone, day of week and hour of day.

okay, i had a detailed discussion with billing team here is the summary of our discussion.What’s happening

* When a driver is migrated from one driver_id to another, the balance is moved as well.
* In data, this shows up as:
** fleet_campaign (supply spend subtype) = 100 EUR: driver got from campaigns
** account_migration_manual (supply spend subtype) = 100 EUR: same driver changed his id and got a new id and then the balance is moved as well.
** account_migration_manual_FEE (revenue subtype) = 100 EUR: which is currently not available in marts.
* So at first glance, it looks like:
** Total spend = 200 EUR
** Total revenue = 100 EUR
** Net = -100 EUR (Bolt spent 100 EUR).

The reality

* In practice, this isn’t really “spend” — it’s just money movement between driver accounts.
* That’s why the subtype {{account_migration_manual_FEE}} isn’t defined in our dbt metrics.
* Net rate calculation is correct because the dashboard uses
** rides_total_revenue_eur_local – rides_total_expense_eur_local which already cancels out these adjustments.
* The only issue is in the supply spend breakdown, where this transaction can look like a double count.

What we should do

* Don’t change the metrics layer (too complex and risky).
* For analysis or reporting:
** Either exclude {{account_migration_manual}} subtype from supply spend.
** Or add a comment/footnote explaining that this isn’t actual spend, just a driver balance transfer.

Simple takeaway:
Net rate is fine. In supply spend breakdown, these entries can look like double counting, but they’re not real spend they’re just money moved between driver accounts. For analysis, exclude or annotate this subtype instead of trying to adjust it in metrics.

Dear Elīna,

Thank you for your data subject rights request from *8 September 2025*, where you raised the concern about an alleged transfer of your child’s personal data to your employer due to linked family account.

Firstly, we would like to clarify that family accounts do not support Bolt Food. Family accounts are only designed for use with rides and rentals.

Secondly, when an individual becomes a member of a family account, their account is created separately and remains their own. Only the payment instrument is linked to all members of family account. This is a card managed by the family account owner, which becomes available as a payment option for the family member.

If your child chooses the family payment method when placing an order, then the family account owner can see the name, spending information and trip/order details for that purchase. However, if your child uses any other payment method –  for example, their own card – this information will not be visible to the family account owner. This ensures that the family member’s account activity is independent, unless they specifically choose to use the shared payment method.

Lastly, we would like to highlight that the family option does not support business payment methods. Only card payments can be added as a family payment instrument.

Your child’s account remains an independent account. For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/lv-lv/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/lv-lv/privacy/|smart-link], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

*Your rights* 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

Yours sincerely, 

Bolt

[~accountid:5b8d306bfa38ae2c89608b95] thank you for clarification.
I just consulted with my legal team, and in this case the question of Bolt’s liability scope is not left to business discretion. Essentially, Bolt cannot assume responsibility for the proper delivery of goods, because doing so would require amending all T&Cs, given that Bolt’s entire operating model is based on the fact that Bolt itself does not appear anywhere as a contracting party. That is, the user concludes a contract with the seller/restaurant, and the user concludes a separate contract with the courier.

Therefore, we cannot change the scope of liability, as this would require changing all other T&Cs (both for the courier and the user).

Similarly, we cannot assume responsibility for reclassification risk — Bolt should avoid wording that creates a direct contractual delivery obligation (otherwise it undermines the independence model).

Taking this into account, my proposal for the agreement would be as follows:

_12.1 Bolt is not liable for the performance of the Sales Agreement nor for any claims presented under the Sales Agreement, including but not limited to in cases of sale and/or handing over of alcoholic beverages or any other Goods controlled under applicable local laws to Clients who are below the required minimum age and only during the times allowed under applicable laws. Thereat, Bolt shall take all reasonable and lawful measures (judicial,technical, and operational) (“Measures”) to ensure that alcoholic beverages would not be sold and/or handed over to the Clients who are below the required minimum age or to the Clients after the times allowed under applicable laws._

_12.1.1. For the avoidance of doubt, Bolt is not responsible for the performance of the Delivery Agreement nor liable for any claims presented in relation thereto. Notwithstanding the foregoing, in the event that Rimi suffers direct, documented, and substantiated losses as a result of (i) a proven failure of Delivery in breach of the Delivery Agreement, and (ii) such failure is not reasonably attributable to Rimi, Bolt may, as a goodwill gesture and without admission of liability, compensate Rimi up to [X]% of such loss, provided that in no event shall Bolt’s total aggregate compensation under this Clause exceed the aggregate sales value generated on Bolt’s Platform from Rimi over the past eight (8) months (“Alcohol Liability Cap”)._

h2. 🛡️ Final Privacy & Legal Advice Summary Bolt Guardian AZ 

*From Alon Alkalay – For the AZ Operations Team*

*Subject: Bolt Guardian – Azerbaijan Launch*

*Source Slack Thread where advice was provided* — [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C08MCQBCY4X/p1752849950752359|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C08MCQBCY4X/p1752849950752359|smart-link] 

----

h3. 🧭 1. Legal Roles & Data Responsibility

In the current Azerbaijan model, *Bolt is the primary data controller* for CCTV footage. This is because:

* Bolt's CS team will monitor CCTV in real-time,
* Bolt has exclusive access to the recordings during and after trips.

Even though storage is handled by GeekBro, they are acting as a *data processor*, not a controller — they support our processing purposes, but do not decide _why_ or _how_ data is used.

The Fleets do not access or manage the footage, so they are *not data controllers*. Even if you were to give Fleets some level of access, that wouldn’t change Bolt’s legal responsibilities. If Bolt accesses or uses the footage, Bolt is responsible for doing so lawfully — even if someone else has access too.

----

h3. 🏛️ 2. Legal Basis for Processing

Under *Decree 183*, all taxis are required to record CCTV footage. That gives us a *legal obligation* that serves as a lawful basis *to record and store video footage without consent*, but only for the following purposes:

* Law enforcement investigations,
* Disputes or incident resolution,
* State security or compliance monitoring.

However, *consent is still required* for any other uses beyond these. That includes the key business features you’re introducing with Bolt Guardian:

* Real-time monitoring by CS,
* Guardian trip alerts or ride-sharing,
* Rider/booker access to recordings,
* Proactive interventions,
* Any additional commercial or operational use.

Put simply: *you cannot rely on the legal obligation under Decree 183 for these features. You will need valid consent.*

----

h3. ✅ 3. Consent Requirements

We previously received local legal advice confirming that *audio recording is not permitted without consent from all passengers*. I expect the same consent standards to apply to CCTV video for features that go beyond legal obligations.

I've asked local counsel to clarify:

* Whether *implied consent* (e.g. choosing the Guardian category or entering a clearly marked vehicle) is enough,
* Or whether *explicit consent* (e.g. ticking a box or clicking a button) is legally required.

I've also asked counsel to clarify how the data protection law interacts with Decree 183 — and whether we could rely on the Decree _instead_ of consent. Once I receive their response, I’ll share it with you.

In parallel, we need to explore *what’s technically feasible in Product* to implement a compliant consent solution.

----

h3. 🧍‍♂️ 4. Consent from Third-Party Passengers

A major issue is obtaining valid consent from *non-booking passengers* — friends, family, children, or others who enter the vehicle with the primary Rider.

Local counsel confirmed (as expected) that *all individuals being recorded must be informed and, in some cases, consent may be required*.

Given that we have *no current way to capture third-party consent in-app*, I’ve advised that the only viable legal mitigation is:

* *Clear, visible in-vehicle signage* that alerts all occupants to CCTV recording, and
* A *QR code linking to Bolt’s Privacy Notice* to provide further transparency.

To be very clear: *you will need both the in-app consent screen and in-vehicle signage*. These are not interchangeable — they serve different functions, and both are required for legal compliance.

----

h3. 📱 5. UX: Consent & Notification Flow

To meet legal standards, I’ve recommended creating a *dedicated in-app consent screen* that:

* Is shown immediately when the Guardian category is selected,
* Includes a clear privacy and consent message,
* Features a button (e.g. _“I Accept”_, _“Continue”_) that must be clicked to proceed,
* *Prevents users from booking* unless that button is clicked,
* *Logs that interaction* (e.g. in Mixpanel or equivalent) as proof of consent.

The button text can vary — it could say “OK”, “Proceed”, or “Continue” — as long as:

* It’s *not possible* to bypass the screen and still book,
* The click is *tracked and timestamped*.

If the user can dismiss the screen by clicking “X” and continue booking, then the consent flow is ineffective and legally insufficient.

----

h3. 📦 6. Storage & Retention

You mentioned that GeekBro will store footage on a *government server*. I’ve reviewed Decree 183 (via GPT translation), and it *requires storage for 30 days*, but does *not mandate* that it be stored on a government-owned server.

Pending final confirmation from local counsel, if they confirm government server storage isn’t a requirement, then I would *strongly recommend (and insist)* that the footage be stored on a *private server*, preferably with safeguards equivalent to AWS or similar.

This is because:

* If the government owns the server, it’s plausible they can access the footage — especially if they hold encryption keys.
* Even if that’s not the intent, the legal and reputational risk remains.

----

h3. 📅 7. Local Legal Advice – Request & Follow-Up

On *18 July*, I formally requested local legal advice on the key issues listed above, including:

* Type of consent required (explicit vs implied),
* Interaction between Decree 183 and data protection law,
* Whether storing on a government server is mandated.

I’ve followed up several times and will share the final advice with you as soon as it arrives.

----

h3. 🚀 8. Pilot Recommendations

I understand the plan is to launch a *3-month pilot* with 200 cars in Azerbaijan.

I’ve advised that we *do not need to block the pilot*, but if the in-app consent and tracking are *not yet implemented*, then *you must accept the legal risk* associated with that decision.

My strong recommendation is:

* Track consent properly as soon as possible,
* And *commit to full compliance* (UX screen + signage + logging) *before any wider launch*.

----

h3. 🛠️ 9. Alternative Consent Approaches (If Full UX is Delayed)

If Product cannot support full UX implementation right now, I suggested some *interim or scalable options* for you to consider:

* Show the consent screen once per *Rider Profile*, e.g., if a parent and child share an account.
* Re-trigger the screen every *X days or rides*.
* Use *in-app Stories* or other contextual surfaces to communicate key legal disclaimers.

These are not substitutes for consent but may help reduce risk and improve transparency if the ideal solution cannot yet be implemented.

----

h3. 🌍 10. Strategic Outlook: Preparing for Other Markets

I want to stress that the privacy and legal issues we’re working through in Azerbaijan will *almost certainly apply in other Bolt Guardian markets*.

I strongly recommend that you:

* Build the UX and legal compliance strategy now in AZ with *scale in mind*,
* Create *reusable templates* for in-app consent, legal text, and signage,
* Treat AZ as the *baseline model* to replicate and adapt elsewhere.

This will save considerable time, resources, and reduce risk when expanding Bolt Guardian globally.

Reopened for an extra fix;

we got this error:


{noformat}[{"field":"totalAmount","originalValue":17,"errorMessage":"(Domestic) totalAmount = salesAmount + FreeTaxSalesAmount + ZeroTaxSalesAmount + TaxAmount."}]{noformat}


Turns out that salesAmount is Tax INCLUDED for b2c and Tax EXCLUDED for b2b. We are b2b. 
SalesAmount should be tax excluded.
Original answer from the partner:

{quote}For B2C eGUIs, salesAmount is tax included and taxAmount is fixed as 0. For B2B eGUIs, salesAmount is tax excluded, as tax must be listed separately and reported as business tax to the government.

 

You may refer to the details in the API Document:

[B2C eGUI issuance|https://gateweb.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PDAK/pages/559251460/Gateweb+Domestic_Test+API+Specifications#Issue-eGui---C0403-B2C] salesAmount  //  [Integer] Sales Amount of the transaction (Tax Included)

[B2B eGUI issuance|https://gateweb.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PDAK/pages/559251460/Gateweb+Domestic_Test+API+Specifications#Issue-eGui---C0403-B2B] salesAmount  // [Integer] Sales Amount of the transaction (Tax Excluded)

 

Since Bolt is issuing only B2B eGUIs at this phase, the definitions apply as follows:

* salesAmount: tax-excluded

* freeTaxSalesAmount and zeroTaxSalesAmount: These apply for products that are free of tax or zero-rated. Please enter their corresponding tax amounts.

* taxAmount: If a product costs TWD 100 before tax and the taxRate is 0.05 (TaxType = 1), then taxAmount = 100 × 0.05 = *5*

* totalAmount: salesAmount + taxAmount. For example, salesAmount TWD 100 + taxAmount 5 = totalAmount *105*

 

Taking your payload as an example, since this is a B2B eGUI, the sales amount should be tax-exclusive. That is, if salesAmount =17 and taxAmount = 1, totalAmount =18 (17+1)

The agreement does not pass review as several terms breach our guidelines.

*Key Terms*

* Term: Indefinite
* Termination Notice Period: 12 months for 1oT's ordinary termination; Customer can terminate at any time without notice
* Governing Law: Estonia
* Jurisdiction: Arbitration Court of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Estonia in Tallinn
* Indemnity: No

*Non-compliant provisions:*

*1 - Warranties:*The agreement lacks a supplier warranties clause covering authority, capacity, valid execution, and performance standards. This leaves critical commitments unaddressed and should include explicit supplier warranties regarding capacity, proper execution, and performance in compliance with industry best practices.

*2 - Compliance with law:*The Agreement fails to impose an obligation on the Supplier to comply with all Applicable Laws or to update the Customer on any legal changes affecting performance. For operational and legal certainty, the Supplier must commit to abiding by all Applicable Laws and provide timely updates on changes.

*3 - Confidentiality:*Section 11 on Confidentiality lacks the mandatory return or destruction obligation and injunctive relief provisions required by the playbook. These additional safeguards are critical to fully protect Bolt's confidential data.

*4 - IP Rights (IPR):*The Agreement lacks comprehensive IP rights provisions, including the assignment of Bespoke IPR and detailed licensing arrangements. This omission materially breaches the playbook requirements and fails to ensure Bolt retains control over all bespoke outputs.

*5 - IP Indemnity:*The Agreement lacks an IP indemnity clause; there is no provision requiring the supplier to indemnify Bolt against intellectual property infringement claims. Without this clause, Bolt may face uncompensated losses in the event of IP infringement claims.

*6 - Audit rights:*The Agreement does not provide the proper audit rights for Bolt; the existing clause only imposes an obligation on the Customer to assist 1oT's audit of its own compliance. This provision does not allow Bolt to verify the supplier's record keeping and compliance.

*7 - Limitation of Liability:*The limitation of liability clause does not meet the playbook requirements; it solely caps the supplier's liability at the fees paid in the preceding 12 months and lacks a fixed minimum cap and necessary unlimited liability carve-outs.

*8 - Change of Control:*The Agreement is missing a Change of Control clause that mandates the supplier to notify Bolt prior to any change of control and to provide related information. This clause is necessary to ensure Bolt can adequately manage risks associated with ownership changes.

*9 - Termination for Cause:*The termination provisions do not clearly address termination for supplier material breach with the required cure period. It is important that termination rights be clearly defined with an opportunity to cure before termination is exercised.

*10 - Termination for Convenience:*The termination clause (Section 10.2) permits unilateral termination by the Customer but fails to specify a defined notice period and the absence of liability. The termination right should include a specified notice period and clarify that no termination compensation applies.

*11 - Consequences of Termination:*The Agreement lacks detailed provisions on the consequences of termination as required by the Bolt review guidance. For clarity and orderly wind-down, the Agreement must detail the consequences, including data and asset return.

*12 - Sub‑contracting:*The Agreement does not contain any provisions addressing subcontracting, contrary to Bolt's requirements. A proper subcontracting clause is essential to ensure that any delegation does not undermine the supplier's obligations.

*13 - Force Majeure:*The Agreement does not include a Force Majeure clause that addresses relief for performance delays or non-performance due to uncontrollable events. This leaves Bolt without the contractual protection envisaged in the review guidance.

*14 - Dispute Resolution:*Section 12.6 mandates immediate final arbitration without a staged dispute resolution process or provisions for continued performance and interim relief. A staged process helps promote early settlement while maintaining service continuity.

*15 - Governing Law and Jurisdiction or Arbitration:*The arbitration clause and jurisdiction provisions do not align with the preferred options set out in the review guidance. The arbitration forum should be revised to align with the approved alternatives to ensure a balanced dispute resolution process.

Thank you,Supplier Agreements Agent

h3. Interpreted Stacktrace

* {{bg_exit_core}} and {{spi_bus_lock_bg_exit}} in {{spi_bus_lock.c}}
These functions are part of the SPI bus locking mechanism in ESP-IDF. They’re responsible for handling SPI bus access in background (BG) mode.
* {{spi_intr}} in {{spi_master.c}}
This is the SPI interrupt handler, which manages SPI transactions and signals completion.
* {{_xt_lowint1}} in {{xtensa_vectors.S}}
This is the low-level interrupt vector handler for Xtensa CPUs.
* {{vPortClearInterruptMaskFromISR}} and {{vPortExitCritical}} in FreeRTOS
These manage interrupt masking and critical section exit in the FreeRTOS kernel.

h3. What does this mean?

* The crash occurs while handling a SPI interrupt (likely after a transaction finishes).
* The {{bg_exit_core}} routine tries to clean up or release the SPI bus.
* The crash happens during or after exiting a critical section ({{vPortExitCritical}}), possibly due to invalid state or memory corruption.

h3. Most Likely Causes

# *SPI Bus Lock Misuse or Double Free*
#* If you call SPI bus release or cleanup routines more than once, or from an invalid context (e.g., not from the expected task or ISR), this can cause memory corruption or assertion failures.
# *ISR Context Issues*
#* If non-IRAM-safe code or memory is accessed from an interrupt context, this can crash the system. All code and data accessed in ISRs must be placed in IRAM (internal RAM).
# *Freertos Critical Section/Interrupt Handling Mistake*
#* If you manually manipulate interrupt masks or critical sections and an interrupt occurs unexpectedly, this can corrupt the FreeRTOS kernel state.
# *Stack Overflow or Corruption*
#* If the interrupt stack or task stack is too small and an overflow occurs, function return addresses or local variables may be corrupted, leading to crashes in routines like {{bg_exit_core}}.
# *SPI Driver or Peripheral Misconfiguration*
#* Misconfigured SPI peripherals or incorrect use of the ESP-IDF SPI API can lead to undefined behavior, especially with bus locking.

h3. What Should You Check?

* *Ensure you’re using the SPI bus lock API correctly:*
** Only call release/exit routines once per transaction.
** Don’t call from outside the intended context (task/ISR).
* *Review your ISR code:*
** Make sure all data/code accessed in ISRs is IRAM-safe.
* *Check stack sizes:*
** Increase ISR and task stack sizes if you suspect overflow.
* *ESP-IDF version:*
** Some ESP-IDF versions have known bugs with SPI bus locking. Make sure you’re using a stable release, and check the ESP-IDF issues for related bugs.
* *Peripheral configuration:*
** Double-check SPI peripheral initialization and bus lock configuration.

----

*If you can share your SPI configuration and how you use bus locking (code snippets), I can give more targeted advice or spot any misuse.*
If you suspect a bug in the ESP-IDF, let me know your version and I can check upstream issues.

I just had a look at the Supplier Terms that you sent.

The Agreement does not pass review as several terms breach our guidelines.

*Key Terms*

* Term: Indefinite
* Termination Notice Period: 30 days
* Governing Law: Sweden
* Jurisdiction: Sweden
* Indemnity: Yes

*Non-compliant provisions:*

*1 - Warranties:*The Agreement lacks an express warranty that the Consultant has full legal capacity, authority, and valid execution to enter into this Agreement. This omission increases the risk of later challenges regarding the Consultant's authority.

*2 - Compliance with law:*The Agreement fails to include the Consultant's obligation to notify Bolt in writing of any changes in Applicable Laws that could impact performance, contrary to our requirement for timely notification of legal changes.

*3 - Confidentiality:*The confidentiality provisions omit required elements including obligations to return/destroy Confidential Information upon request with certification, and explicit statements on injunctive relief, undermining comprehensive protection of Bolt's information.

*4 - Publicity:*The Agreement lacks restrictions on making public announcements or using Bolt's name, trademarks, or brand materials without prior written consent, leaving Bolt's brand unprotected against unauthorized publicity.

*5 - IP Rights (IPR):*Clause 7.4 is overbroad, requiring assignment of all existing and future IPRs without preserving the Consultant's pre-existing (Supplier Background) IPR, contrary to our requirement that only bespoke IPR be assigned.

*6 - IP Indemnity:*Clause 12.6 lacks key elements such as supplier control of defence subject to Bolt's consent, mandatory remediation of infringing deliverables, and a refund mechanism if remediation fails.

*7 - Audit rights:*The Agreement omits essential audit provisions for record-keeping, access to records and systems, and audit procedures, preventing Bolt from verifying the Consultant's compliance.

*8 - Limitation of Liability:*While the Agreement caps Bolt's liability, it fails to set a corresponding limitation on the Consultant's aggregate liability, leaving Bolt exposed to potentially unlimited losses.

*9 - Standard Indemnity:*Clause 12.6 is overly broad, covering all losses without limiting it to material breaches, and lacks a clear cap and linkage to Bolt's general liability cap.

*10 - Change of Control:*Clause 4.1.13 only requires "prompt written notice" of change of control instead of the required 60-day prior notice and detailed risk assessment information.

*11 - Termination for Cause:*Clause 3.2.1 uses a 7-day cure period for material breach instead of the required 30 days and omits a supplier termination right for Bolt's non-payment.

*12 - Force Majeure:*Clause 13.5 allows termination after more than 15 days instead of the required 14 days and does not grant Bolt the right to suspend payments or engage a third party for unperformed services.

*13 - Dispute Resolution:*The Agreement lacks a staged dispute resolution process beginning with informal discussions and escalating through representatives, mediation, and finally court proceedings.

*14 - Governing Law and Jurisdiction:*Clauses 25.1 and 25.2 mandate Swedish law and courts, which does not align with Bolt's preferred legal forum options of Estonian law, local Bolt entity jurisdiction, or England and Wales.

Thank you,Supplier Agreements Agent

Hi [~accountid:61e918be38041c00686ad2bf], thank you for raising this ticket in light of the DDPP audit last year. 



# *Category Description & Naming*

* In June 2024, the DDPP issued warnings regarding misleading consumer communication in both the "Comfort" and "Taxi" categories. That criticism concerned the potential for deceptive representations, which contravene the principles of the _code de la consommation_, particularly the requirement for clarity and transparency. The naming of “All Cars” is misleading because it excludes other categories (Van, Taxi, Premium etc).
* *Recommendation*: Ensure your category name and description leave no room for ambiguity. Rename “All Cars” to something more descriptive, for instance “_Any Vehicles – Standard or Comfort_” or “_Flexible Vehicle Options._”


# *Pricing Transparency & Estimated Range*

* In the DDPP’s Taxi category review, the issue wasn’t the use of a price bracket per se, but the discrepancy when the actual taximeter fare surpassed the maximum estimate shown—this was deemed a misleading practice.
* That specific issue does not apply here, since the price range reflects distinct categories with differing pricing—not a single measurement that could exceed the shown maximum.
* *Recommendation*: Be very explicit in-app about the purpose of the price range:
** E.g., “Estimated fare reflects the range between Standard and Comfort rates—final price depends on the matched driver’s cate.”
** This aligns with the DDPP's focus on providing clear, non-misleading information about what users should expect.
** Please ensure that if there are any surges applied to a category, this should be reflected on the price bracket shown for the Multiple Category Option - riders could feel misled if the final price exceeds the maximum amount displayed.


# *Price Components Visibility*

* In France, Bolt does not share detailed price component breakdowns (e.g., base fare, per-minute, per‑km) are not publicly displayed within categories (outside of taxis). You can see here the price indications per city where Bolt operates: [https://bolt.eu/fr-fr/cities/|https://bolt.eu/fr-fr/cities/|smart-link]
* *Recommendation*: In order to remain consistent across categories, do *not* expose individual pricing components (e.g., breakdown of Standard vs. Comfort fare elements) within the category detail screen. Re-introducing components here could undermine the approach we have taken in other categories and invite regulatory criticism. Stick with the price range only.

h3. 1. Immediate Clarifications Needed

Before proceeding, could you please confirm the following:

* Have we received any response from *NUISIPROS FRANCE*, the fleet that received the incorrect payout?
* What information did *NUISIPROS* receive with the payment? Specifically, did they receive any banking details belonging to *JCT*?
** If so, we need to involve the *Privacy team* immediately to assess whether a personal data breach occurred.
* Have you confirmed with Central Billing team or Commerce that there is no internal standardised process to rectify this type of payment error?

h3. 2. Legal Basis for Recovery

French civil law provides a clear legal framework for recovering unduly paid amounts:

* *Article 1302 Civil Code*: “Any payment presupposes a debt; what has been received without being owed is subject to restitution.”
* *Article 1302-1 Civil Code*: Restitution is due even if the payment was made by mistake of the payer.
* *Article 1302-3 Civil Code*: Restitution is subject to Articles 1352 to 1352-9, and may be reduced if the payment was made in error.

In short, the wrong fleet has a legal obligation to repay the funds.

h3. 3. Recommended Recovery Options

*A. Forcing a Response from the Wrong Fleet*

* Send formal written notices (registered letter or email with delivery receipt) requiring repayment within a set deadline.
* If unresponsive, escalate to *legal recovery proceedings* (e.g., injunctive relief, debt collection). This is resource-intensive and time-consuming.
* If the fleet is still active, we can also apply *contractual leverage* (suspension or termination clauses) to encourage repayment.

*B. Withholding/Offsetting Future Payouts*

* If the wrong fleet continues generating earnings, we can withhold or offset payouts against the misallocated amount.
* This is often the most effective and practical recovery method, as it avoids litigation.
* We should confirm with Finance/Commerce whether the systems can accommodate offsets and ensure contractual compliance before proceeding.

*C. Ensuring Payment to the Correct Fleet*

* The correct fleet must not be penalized for this error.
* *We recommend issuing their payment independently, while we pursue recovery from the wrong fleet.*

If you need a *report*, please refer to FleetX (DriverX). If your request concerns an *invoice*, follow these steps:

1. Open the **Client page in Admin**: [link|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-rides/clients?tz=Europe%2FTallinn&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D].
2. Enter the Fleet or Driver ID in the **External ID** filter field.
3. Open the driver or fleet profile.
4. Go to the **Invoice tasks** tab.
   * If you see *Invoice sum too small*, no commission invoice was generated because the driver either owed no commission or had more compensation than commission.
   * If you encounter any other error, please let us know.
5. Commission invoices for the entire history of the fleet/driver are available either under **Invoice tasks** or **Partner Invoices**.

I understand your concern; however, I respectfully disagree that regional legal teams are not permitted to communicate with data protection authorities in their respective markets due to the risk of inspection. While such a risk may exist in other countries, it is not the case in Latvia when you approach authorities with general questions and do not disclose any particularly sensitive non-compliance issues. My approach across the Baltics is to reach out to authorities when I have questions - I can assess whether the matter is too sensitive and could backfire if raised, or whether it is a general compliance question where consultation with the authority is appropriate.

From my experience, authorities in the Baltics highly appreciate when companies proactively seek guidance. It is never treated as a trigger for investigation — on the contrary, it helps us build a relationship and present ourselves as a responsible company. That was exactly the case here.

That said, in the future, I will inform the Privacy Team in advance if I intend to reach out to data protection authorities in any of my markets and will seek your confirmation beforehand. Thank you!

My conclusions for this issue are following:

The issue lies within the IoT main regulator BQ25798 “poor source detection” feature. 

When battery is unplugged and the 24V regulator in the controller is turned off, the energy stored in the capacitors and inductors on the 24V line starts to oscillate - components on both IoT and controller contribute to this. The energy fades out in about 15 seconds after the battery is unplugged and only then the 24V line reaches 0V. When the battery is connected after 24V line has reached 0V, the IoT boots normally.

The solution would be a feature, which dumps the leftover energy from the 24V after the battery is removed. 

Short term solutions would be as follows:

# Without doing any rework - implement firmware fix: Delay battery output turn on 15 seconds after the battery is inserted into the scooter.
## Downside is long boot-up time for the vehicle, which will affect battery swappers and mechanics to some extent.
# Install 1.7k resistor on 24V line delay battery output turn on for 3 seconds.
## This solution decreases the 15s 24V discharge time from 15s to about 6s which mitigates the problem but does not solve it completely. Adding a longer battery output turn on time can ensure that during battery swap, the 24V line is discharged to 0V.
## Big downside of this solution is that 0.3W of idle current is constantly added to the vehicle and this reduces the uptime of the first 600 vehicles.
# Do nothing - rely on the back-up battery during battery swaps and hope that the problem does not occur very often.
## There will definitely be cases where the IoT’s will be detected as faulty by mechanics when testing something in the warehouse and working IoTs will probably get thrown away.

Long term solutions:

# Get rid of the “poor source detection” feature on BQ25798 or use another main power regulator.
## D1 IoT main regulator does not have this feature and there have not been any power supply issues for D1 IoT. (The 24V regulator in the controller for D1 and EB1 is the same)
## There is always a risk that some “glitches” will happen for the scooter, the worst that during user orders, too high recharge current or other similar events, which are not allowed by the battery can cut the power to the scooter for short time. This could cause the ride to end for the user if the BB is not working. In my opinion the regulator should be more robust and this “poor input” feature seems to not suit our application.
# Implement “power good” circuit to the IoT which only enables 24V to IoT if the voltage is detected as “good” for the IoT.
## The current testing set up does not have AI cameras etc attached - all components added to the 24V (or downward the 24V) later on will influence the 24V line behavior, there it might not be possible to just fix the issue on the controller side. 
# Implement discharge circuit on the 24V line when battery is removed
## If the battery is removed, a circuit on the 24V line will be active which will quickly discharge the excess energy. - similar to the short term solution 2 but the constant idle drain is removed.
## This solution might not solve the issue completely as the battery pre-charge also influences the transient process for the 24V line. It can be improved but it’s more complicated to make it “perfect”.

{code:sql}WITH
  latest_request_per_user AS (
    SELECT
      user_id,
      user__created_age_in_days,
      user_payments__successful_cash_payments,
      user_payments__successful_payments,
      created AS last_request_date
    FROM(
        SELECT
          r.user_id,
          r.user__created_age_in_days,
          r.user_payments__successful_cash_payments,
          r.user_payments__successful_payments,
          r.created,
          ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY r.user_id ORDER BY r.created DESC) AS rn
        FROM
          glue.ng_pii.etl_user_order_request AS r
        WHERE
          r.created_date >= DATE_ADD('week', -1, CURRENT_DATE)
      )
    WHERE rn = 1
  ),
  peak_cancellation_day AS (
SELECT
user_id,
cancellation_date,
daily_cancelled_orders
    FROM
      (SELECT
          user_id,
          cancellation_date,
          daily_cancelled_orders,
          ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY daily_cancelled_orders DESC, cancellation_date DESC) AS rn
        FROM
(SELECT
etl.user_id,
CAST(etl.created AS DATE) AS cancellation_date,
COUNT(etl.order_id) AS daily_cancelled_orders
            FROM
              ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
              INNER JOIN ng_public.company_order_try AS cot ON cot.order_id = etl.order_id AND cot.city_id = etl.city_id AND cot.client_cancel_reason IS NOT NULL
            WHERE
              etl.created_date >= DATE_ADD('week', -1, CURRENT_DATE)
              AND cot.created_date >= DATE_ADD('week', -1, CURRENT_DATE)
              AND etl.city_id = 666
              AND etl.country_code = 'ae'
              AND etl.order_state <> 'finished'
            GROUP BY
              1, 2 )
)
    WHERE rn = 1
  )
SELECT
  pcd.user_id,
  pcd.cancellation_date AS peak_day,
  pcd.daily_cancelled_orders AS peak_day_cancellations,
  CONCAT('https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/', CAST(pcd.user_id AS varchar)) AS user_link,
  latest.user__created_age_in_days,
  latest.user_payments__successful_cash_payments,
  latest.user_payments__successful_payments,
  latest.last_request_date,
  uu.is_blocked
FROM

Unfortunately, the customers refunds are failing with an error response code 59 and PAYMENT_ERROR_FRAUD (327)	

The customer payments team has checked with SilverFlow if we would be able to issue the refunds again. Unfortunately, we are not able to retry the refunds as the customers bank is rejecting the funds. We would only be able to issue to refund to the Bolt Balance in this case. 

SilverFlow was not able to advise what exactly is causing the refund to fail, but provided some common scenarios. 

Below you can find some common scenarios for response code 59 for refunds:

* Unusual refund patterns or amounts
* Refunds to cards that have been flagged for suspicious activity
* Refunds that don't match typical merchant behavior patterns
* Cross-border refund transactions that trigger geographic risk rules
* Refunds processed outside normal business hours or patterns
* Multiple refund attempts in short time periods

The issuer's fraud detection system analyses various risk factors and if the refund transaction is deemed suspicious but not definitively fraudulent, response code 59 is the appropriate decline code to use.

Let me know if you have any questions. 

Cheers, 
Marten

_Yours sincerely,_

*Proposed to Mirjam and Samantha:*

To highlight urgency and the threat of regulatory action, I’ve added an extra column in the [Rides Monthly review sheet|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1IoVhnqYrYa9iUS8Xfwi3I7K4jwd-b3kSGDFGaSFBpNc/edit?tab=t.0] and revised the [Operational Compliance Jira Board project|https://docs.google.com/document/d/14YrqoYlHtwiDd6WZ1epgwIyuddCNdC-5pGrU4r0Adf4/edit?tab=t.0] to ensure the legal questionnaire captures that aspect as well:

* Regulatory Action Risk: How likely is it that this issue could trigger regulatory action (audit, fine, litigation) based on Bolt’s past exposure and the probability of such action in the future? Has it already occurred?

This means that instead of changing the risk assessment methodology (risk event impact x likelihood of risk event occurring), we layer this additional _urgency_ metric on top of the existing process to highlight potential or impending regulatory responses. Gregory has informed me that Anett will have capacity to set up the Jira board for us in the next couple of weeks, so we can start tracking info on those requests more effectively

On the issue of every case scoring as *Significant risk*:

The current process and legal questionnaire were designed specifically for prioritising *country-level regulatory issues*, where risks stem from legislation or enforcement of compliance obligations at a local level. For *foundational/admin resiliency topics*, we should create a *separate risk assessment questionnaire* tailored to technical risks of global scale, developed with Engineering, InfoSec, and IT alongside Legal. This will ensure we properly frame and score these risks, including their long-term impact.

* *Done* - Create API for live courier multipliers from pricing service

* *In-progress -* Store live courier multipliers in both remote config and DB
** To migrate courier multipliers from Remote Config to our owned database, we’ll run a short dual-write phase that saves updates to both data stores before cutting over
** Updates will be done by leveraging existing admin panel endpoints for scheduled multipliers
** This path allows us to switch consumers one by one and avoid outages since a fallback is available

The problem is most likely that the common mode noise does not have a low impedance path to GND, which causes the voltage levels to shift.

After discussion with Genfo, it was decided to add capacitors to all sensor signal lines and supply lines to provide the low impedance path for the “noise” to be suppressed.

This in general seems to be very similar problem what the rear brake light had with it’s signal line, adding a capacitor to controller output helped to solve the problem. I think that it was somehow “lucky” that this test was passed during the initial EMC testing in Dekra. Probably the values are on edge and slight deviation in the set up either causes or prevents this problem from happening. For example the vehicle angle in relation to the antenna used in the test.

What the TVDE Law prohibits is for the platform operator to own TVDE vehicles, finance or be an interested party in the purchase, rental, leasing or other form of use of TVDE vehicles.
Considering that Bolt has no involvement in the purchase or delivery of this vehicle, i.e. the vehicle is assigned directly by the brand, then this situation does not fall within the scope of these prohibitions.
However, we believe it is necessary to draw up some short T&Cs for this, similar to those of Uber, and for that we need to know the car and brand, the conditions of participation and how the winner is chosen. In the T&Cs, we will safeguard that the allocation of the car is the sole responsibility of the brand, thus safeguarding our position.

Hello [~accountid:5e4fb3b04d2a000c9114bc04], thank you for this information. 


Our SE rider T&C state, that “4.7. Om du har beställt transporttjänster genom Bolt-appen och skadar förarens fordon eller dess utrustning (bland annat genom att orsaka fläckar eller missfärgningar, eller orsaka att fordonet blir illaluktande), ska föraren ha rätt till att begära en straffavgift av dig upp till 500 SEK, samt begära kompensation för eventuella skador som överskrider straffavgiften. Om du inte betalar straffavgiften och/eller ersätter skadorna, kan Bolt inkassera anspråken för transporttjänsteleverantörs räkning.”. Which means driver can ask for fine up to 500 SEK, as well as claim compensation for any damages exceeding the penalty fee. 

In this case, we have the driver’s photos showing that body fluids contaminated both the inside and outside of the vehicle, as well as areas such as the gaps between windows and other hard-to-reach places, which are difficult to clean. Therefore, in my opinion, the driver should have the right to claim the specified compensation, since it is likely that the car required professional cleaning due to both possible odor and contamination.

I am not fully comfortable with the fact that the information about the requested amounts, which you shared via the link, is more of our internal guidance and not reflected in the T&C. If this information were included in the T&C, we would not have to engage in so many disputes with riders in such situations.

Our answer to the rider could look something like this:

Dear [Riders name],

We are sorry to hear that you felt unwell during your trip.

Please note that under Bolt General Terms and Conditions for Passengers clause 4.7:
_“If you have ordered transport services through the Bolt app and damage the driver’s vehicle or its equipment (including, for example, by causing stains or discoloration, or causing the vehicle to become malodorous), the driver shall have the right to claim a penalty fee from you of up to SEK 500, as well as claim compensation for any damages exceeding the penalty fee. If you do not pay the penalty fee and/or compensate the damages, Bolt may collect the claims on behalf of the transport service provider.”_

In this case, the driver submitted photos to Bolt showing that body fluids had contaminated both the interior and exterior of the vehicle. As the contamination extended to gaps between windows and other hard-to-reach areas, the driver had the right to claim SEK 2,000 to cover the costs of professional interior cleaning.

If you believe that you were mistakenly charged twice, or that the driver intentionally took a longer route leading to additional costs, we kindly ask you to provide any supporting evidence (e.g. screenshots, route comparisons). We will make sure to review the matter further.

Thank you for your understanding.

Kind regards,

Hi [~accountid:712020:96f9e924-98dd-4ef5-a7da-0752de9a24ce], apologies for the delay. I do not recommend proceeding with Bolt Lux in Lithuania for the following reasons:

# *No fleets in Lithuania.* Under the law, all ride-hailing drivers are self-employed individuals. Since there are no fleets employing RH drivers that could contract directly with Bolt (and thus mitigate reclassification risk), Bolt would need to impose quality criteria and monitor driver compliance directly. This creates high reclass risk.
# *Political will to reclassify drivers.* Lithuania is one of the pioneer countries in the EU moving quickly with the implementation of the PWD. An amendment law is already in place under discussion with seven employment criteria, and there is a strong political will to reclassify drivers. Any additional requirements or restrictions would only add to the debate, which is already not in our favor.
# *Taxi category option (limited).* The only potential workaround would be to launch a limited version of Bolt Lux within the taxi category, as there are taxi fleets employing drivers. However, the share of taxi providers on the Bolt Platform in Lithuania is only around 2–3%, so this option is unlikely to be scalable.

Let me know if you have any further questions.
